sourceFacts: Dystrophinopathies characteristically cause greater proximal than distal weakness.
Describing anatomical weakness distribution helps clinical localisation.
prompt:
Create a polished original medical teaching illustration in landscape 3:2 format. Use the attached MD3 original solely as a style reference: warm watercolour/gouache on an ivory paper background, delicate ink contours, calm navy labels, muted ochre/peach/teal colours, generous whitespace and clear flat anatomical shapes. Anatomical clarity before decoration. Never photorealistic skin, glossy blood, wet flesh, fat lobules, scary faces, chunky 3D tissue blocks, or a fake scan. Only exact requested labels, clean legible short text. Footer 'Educational schematic'. No watermark, logos or attribution in the pixels. Compose an entirely new subject from the clinical specification, not the scalp content in the reference.

Two full-body front-view simple modest child silhouettes in fitted plain T-shirt and leggings, symmetrical neutral stance and flat colours. Do not show skin muscles or organs. Left labelled 'Proximal pattern': semi-transparent teal highlights on BOTH shoulder/upper-arm areas and BOTH hips/upper-thigh areas, hands and feet unhighlighted. Right labelled 'Distal pattern': ochre highlights on BOTH forearm/hand and lower-leg/foot areas, shoulder and hips unhighlighted. Fine callouts left 'Shoulder and hip girdles'; right 'Hands and feet'. Title 'Where is the weakness?'. Bottom 'Distribution helps localise the problem'. No claim that any pattern proves a diagnosis, no disability caricature, no naked children.
